newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - NZ XI slump badly in second innings.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - NZ XI slump badly in second innings.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, Jan 16 - The Selection XI slumped badly in their second innings on the fourth and final day of their cricket match against England.
Matt Horne got a leading edge as he tried to turn Phil Tufnell to the on side and Nick Knight clung onto a reflex catch, after a prolonged juggle, at silly point.
Mark Greatbatch went on the offensive, thumping his third ball from Tufnell for six over mid wicket. The next ball was crunched to the extra cover boundary.
But in the following over he was called for a short single to mid off by Blair Pocock and was beaten by substitute fielder Jack Russell's direct hit.
His 10 had taken just five balls and five minutes.
When Justin Vaughan edged Silverwood to Knight at second slip, having made one, three wickets had fallen in 22 balls.
Earlier, Adam Parore was caught behind off Silverwood for 13.
After 42 overs, the Selection 11 were 85-5, with Pocock on 34 and Llorne Howell on four. They still trailed England by 204 runs.
